description: CHANGE_TRACKING through the SQL surface (the change_tracking cell of SHOW TABLES): a fresh table is OFF; the CREATE TABLE option, ALTER ... SET, or creating a stream turns it ON (and it survives the stream); the CHANGES clause requires it - an untracked table refuses with the single-line wording - and a CHANGES point is bounded by the table's creation (the retention wording) and must be a CONSTANT. Converted 1:1 from features/ChangeTrackingTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE STREAM ct_s ON TABLE ct_streamed
ALTER TABLE ct_alter SET CHANGE_TRACKING = TRUE
ALTER TABLE ct_alter SET CHANGE_TRACKING = FALSE
CREATE TABLE ct_opt (id INTEGER) CHANGE_TRACKING = TRUE
SELECT * FROM ct_plain CHANGES (INFORMATION => DEFAULT) AT (OFFSET => 0)

error.messageContains: Change tracking is not enabled or has been missing for the time range requested on table 'TEST_DB.TEST_SCHEMA.CT_PLAIN'.

steps.sql: ALTER TABLE ct_toggled SET CHANGE_TRACKING = TRUE
ALTER TABLE ct_toggled SET CHANGE_TRACKING = FALSE
SELECT * FROM ct_toggled CHANGES (INFORMATION => DEFAULT) AT (OFFSET => 0)
ALTER TABLE ct_ok SET CHANGE_TRACKING = TRUE
SELECT * FROM ct_ok CHANGES (INFORMATION => DEFAULT) AT (OFFSET => 0)
SELECT * FROM ct_ok CHANGES (INFORMATION => APPEND_ONLY) AT (OFFSET => 0)
CREATE TABLE ct_bound (id INTEGER) CHANGE_TRACKING = TRUE
SELECT * FROM ct_bound CHANGES (INFORMATION => DEFAULT) AT (OFFSET => -86400)

error.messageContains: Time travel data is not available for table CT_BOUND. The requested time is either beyond the allowed time travel period or before the object creation time.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE ct_const (id INTEGER) CHANGE_TRACKING = TRUE
SELECT * FROM ct_const CHANGES (INFORMATION => DEFAULT) AT (TIMESTAMP => DATEADD(minute, -30, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()))

error.messageContains: argument TIMESTAMP to function AT needs to be constant
